question.prompt: One of the following numbers is not divisible by any prime number less than \(10.\) Which is it?

solutions.title: Check the short power cycles
solutions.explanation:
The only primes below \(10\) are \(2,3,5,7\). Checking remainders modulo these four numbers lets us test choice C without evaluating its enormous value.

Let \(N=2^{607}-1\). Since \(N\) is odd, it is not divisible by \(2\). We write \(u\equiv v\pmod m\) when \(u\) and \(v\) have the same remainder upon division by \(m\).

For division by \(3\), note that \(2^2\equiv1\pmod3\). Because \(607=2\cdot303+1\),
\[
2^{607}=(2^2)^{303}\cdot2\equiv2\pmod3,
\]
so \(N\equiv1\pmod3\).

For division by \(5\), use \(2^4\equiv1\pmod5\) and \(607=4\cdot151+3\):
\[
2^{607}=(2^4)^{151}\cdot2^3\equiv8\equiv3\pmod5.
\]
Thus \(N\equiv2\pmod5\).

For division by \(7\), use \(2^3\equiv1\pmod7\) and \(607=3\cdot202+1\):
\[
2^{607}=(2^3)^{202}\cdot2\equiv2\pmod7.
\]
Thus \(N\equiv1\pmod7\).

None of these remainders is zero, so \(\boxed{2^{607}-1}\) is not divisible by any prime below \(10\). The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

solutions.title: Find factors in four choices
solutions.explanation:
Four choices can be eliminated by recognizing factors of differences of powers and sums of odd powers.

For an integer \(r\ge2\),
\[
u^r-v^r=(u-v)(u^{r-1}+u^{r-2}v+\cdots+v^{r-1}).
\]
Expanding the right side cancels all intermediate terms. In particular, \(u-v\) divides \(u^r-v^r\). If \(r\) is odd, replacing \(v\) by \(-v\) also shows that \(u+v\) divides \(u^r+v^r\).

Apply these facts as follows:

| Choice | Rewriting | Prime divisor below \(10\) |
|---|---|---:|
| A | \(2^{606}-1=8^{202}-1^{202}\) | \(8-1=7\) |
| B | \(2^{606}+1=4^{303}+1^{303}\) | \(4+1=5\) |
| D | \(2^{607}+1=2^{607}+1^{607}\) | \(2+1=3\) |
| E | \(2^{607}+3^{607}\) | \(2+3=5\) |

The first row uses a difference of powers. The other three use sums with odd exponents \(303\), \(607\), and \(607\), respectively.

Thus A, B, D, and E each have a prime divisor below \(10\). The question states that exactly one choice avoids all such prime divisors, so the remaining number is \(\boxed{2^{607}-1}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
